script: Entitled kids think they can play with my girlfriend's crutches. Last night, my girlfriend and I went out to eat at a popular dive bar. The place is known for fried chicken that actually tastes like a hug and a raccoon colony that thinks it owns the floor. She's got a shattered foot, so I thought a night out would lift her spirits—if only we could snag a window seat. The bar's windows are huge, and watching the raccoons raid the table scraps is a vibe. I've snagged that view only a couple of times in my life. People usually keep their distance, or if they're photogenic, they snap a pic and move on. It's basically a safe zone for us. But the bar was a circus that night. Kids, parents, late summer heat, and baby raccoons everywhere. We were right by the window—me back to the glass, her facing the corner. The first few kids poked and prodded my space, and I was like, "Okay, fine, they're kids." Their parents were chill, probably just hoping to enjoy a night without a full‑blown zoo. Then the big family—this one had a three‑year‑old, a six‑year‑old, and a ten‑year‑old—started banging on the window with their fists. The kind of noise that would scare a fish tank. Right next to my ear. I was thinking a third‑grader should know better, but they didn't care. The parents were watching, disinterested, no intervention. I kept my cool, because I am a total legend at handling drama. The bar was a dive, but I was a boss. She noticed my face and offered to switch. "I am more comfortable with kids in my space," she said, because she's got a cast and I am not. I thought, "Great, no one will touch those crutches." I slid her crutches to the side of the table, hoping the kids would stay away from her. And then it hit me—there were still two boys just behind her, fiddling with the crutches, peeking through the metal, touching the handles. My jaw dropped. I made eye contact with the mom, who stared straight through me like I was invisible, and with the parents behind my girlfriend, who were as shocked as I was. The youngest was acting all nonchalant, the older one was just staring. My girlfriend turned to them and said, "Hey, can you please not touch those? These are medical aids, and I need them to walk. My foot is broken." They gave her a blank stare. No shame. The little one even asked, "Oh, crutches?" as he pulled the rubber handle. The older one said nothing. My girlfriend stayed calm but firm. They stared for a sec, then wandered back to their seats. I looked again, and the mom was glaring like she wanted lasers out of her eyes. My girlfriend turned to confirm, and the mom was glaring at her too. The mood was ruined, and it felt like a personal attack on my girlfriend's dignity. We left shortly after, but they left faster. No apology, no guilt, just pure entitlement. They'd probably walk into a store and start touching a stroller, like it's a toy. Bestie, I can't even finish the next part because—
